# MCP Tools Reference

The Asana V2 MCP server exposes a set of tools that allow AI assistants to read from and write to your Asana workspace. This page describes the tools, what they do, and when to use them. Availability and tool versions can vary by client and rollout. Use `tools/list` in your connected client to see which tools are available to your session.

> **This list changes over time.** Tools may be added, updated, or deprecated as the tool set evolves. Always use the `tools/list` MCP command in your client to get the current tool schemas. Subscribe to the [developer changelog](https://forum.asana.com/c/forum-en/api/api-changelog/204) for update notifications.

##
**How to use this reference**

Tools are grouped into three categories:

- **Read tools** return data from your workspace without making any changes.
- **Write tools** create, modify, or delete data in your workspace.
- **Interactive tools** display task search results or let you review a task or project before creating it. Availability depends on whether the client supports interactive apps.

**Access and permissions:** MCP apps in Asana do not use permission scopes. When a user authorizes an MCP client, the token automatically requests full access to all available tools. Once authorized, a tool cannot access projects, tasks, or data that the authenticated user does not already have permission to view in Asana.

##
**Read tools**

| Tool | Description | Example prompts |
|---|---|---|
| `search_objects` | Searches tasks, projects, project templates, portfolios, goals, teams, users, tags, custom fields, and AI Teammates by name. Use this first when you do not know an object's GID. Use `resource_type: project_template` to find project templates, `goal` to find goals, `agent` for AI Teammates, or `actor` for humans and AI Teammates together. | "Find the onboarding project template" / "Find the AI Teammate named Triage Bot" |
| `get_task` | Returns task details, including assignee, dates, custom fields, projects, dependencies, followers, parent, and section memberships. Comments and subtasks are included by default and can be excluded with `include_comments` or `include_subtasks`. Use `comment_limit` to control the number of comments returned. | "Show me the details of this task" / "What are the subtasks on the Website Redesign task?" |
| `get_task_stories` | Returns the activity feed for one task or multiple tasks, including comments and system activity such as assignments, completion, and date changes. Use `task_id` for a single task or `task_ids` for a batch. Pagination with `offset` is available only for a single task. Additional filters and sorting depend on the schema returned by `tools/list`. | "What changed on this task?" / "Summarize activity across these tasks" |
| `get_tasks` | Lists tasks by project, section, tag, user task list, or workspace and assignee. Supports modification and completion date filters, pagination, and `opt_fields`. Use `completed_since: now` for incomplete tasks. | "List all incomplete tasks in the Marketing project" / "Show me tasks assigned to me that were modified this week" |
| `get_my_tasks` | Returns tasks assigned to the authenticated user. Supports pagination and `completed_since`. Use `completed_since: now` for incomplete tasks, omit it for all tasks, or provide a timestamp to include tasks completed since that time. | "What tasks do I have?" / "Show me my incomplete tasks" |
| `get_notifications` | Lists Inbox notifications for the authenticated user in the workspace. Includes who triggered each notification and the related work objects. Supports pagination; request `opt_fields: story.text` for the underlying comment or activity text. Available when notification tools are enabled for your session; check `tools/list`. | "What needs my attention in Inbox?" / "What happened while I was away?" |
| `search_tasks` | Advanced task search with full-text and complex filters. Searches task names, descriptions, and comments. Supports filtering by assignee, due date, creation date, project, section, tag, and custom fields. Available on Premium accounts only; use `get_tasks` for non-Premium workspaces. | "Find all overdue tasks assigned to me" / "Search for tasks mentioning 'API redesign' due this month" |
| `get_project` | Returns project details, including owner, members, current status, task counts, and optionally sections. A null task count or sections value means the data could not be retrieved, rather than zero tasks or no sections. | "Show me the details of the Product Launch project" / "What sections does Sprint 12 have?" |
| `get_projects` | Lists projects in the workspace, optionally filtered by team or archive status. Returns task counts by default; use `opt_fields` for other fields such as owner or members. Use `search_objects` to find projects by name. Null task counts mean counts could not be retrieved. | "List all active projects" / "Show me projects for the Engineering team" |
| `get_portfolio` | Returns details for a portfolio by GID. Use `opt_fields` to request additional fields, and `get_items_for_portfolio` to list its contents. | "Show me the details of the Q4 portfolio" |
| `get_portfolios` | Returns a list of portfolios owned by the authenticated user in the current workspace. | "What portfolios do I own?" / "List all my portfolios" |
| `get_items_for_portfolio` | Returns the items inside a portfolio, including projects and goals with their names and IDs. | "What projects are in the Company Goals portfolio?" / "List the items in this portfolio" |
| `get_status_overview` | Returns an aggregated status report for one or more projects or portfolios based on keyword search. Includes project details, current status updates, task summaries, and flagged blockers. This tool handles its own search internally — do not chain other search tools before calling it. | "Give me a status overview of the Rebrand initiative" / "What's the current status of Q2 planning?" |
| `get_attachments` | Returns attachments for a task, project, or project brief. Includes file names, download URLs, and view URLs. | "What files are attached to this task?" / "Show me the attachments on the Design Spec project" |
| `get_user` | Returns details for a user by GID, email address, or the string `"me"`. Returns name, email, and workspace memberships. When called without a user identifier, returns the authenticated user. | "Who am I authenticated as?" |
| `get_me` | Returns the name, email, and workspace memberships of the currently authenticated user. Use when you need specific details about the authenticated user rather than just their GID. | "What account am I logged in as?" / "Show me my user details" |
| `get_users` | Lists users in the workspace, optionally filtered by team membership. Returns GID, name, and email by default; use `opt_fields` to request additional fields. | "Who is on the Engineering team?" / "List users in the workspace" |
| `get_teams` | Returns a list of teams in the workspace. Optionally filter to only teams a specific user belongs to. | "List all teams in the workspace" / "What teams is this user a member of?" |
| `get_agent` | Returns the full record for a single AI Teammate agent by GID. Includes name, description, behavior guidance, workspace, and photo. Use `get_workspace_agents` first to discover agent GIDs, then call this tool for full details on a specific agent. | "Show me the details of this AI Teammate" / "What does the Triage Bot agent do?" |
| `get_workspace_agents` | Returns a list of AI Teammate agents configured in the workspace. Each record includes GID, name, resource type, and resource subtype. Use this to discover available AI Teammates before fetching full details with `get_agent`. Supports pagination. Note: this returns AI Teammates only — not human users. Use `get_users` for people. | "What AI Teammates are configured in this workspace?" / "List all available agents" |
| `get_table` | Returns a single table by GID. Set `include_custom_field_settings` to also return the table's custom field schema as a paginated `custom_field_settings` object; use `custom_field_settings_limit` and `custom_field_settings_offset` to page through it. | "Show me the details of this table" / "What fields does the Vendors table have?" |
| `get_tables` | Lists tables in the workspace. Supports pagination with `limit` and `offset`, and `opt_fields` for additional fields. | "List all tables in the workspace" |
| `get_record` | Returns a single record by GID. Includes the record's comments by default as a paginated `comments` object; set `include_comments` to `false` to omit them. Use `comment_limit` to control how many comments are returned and `comment_offset` to page through the rest. | "Show me the details of this record" / "What comments are on this record?" |
| `get_records` | Lists the records in a table. Requires the table GID. Supports `modified_since` filtering, sorting by `created_at`, and pagination. | "List all records in the Vendors table" / "Show records modified since last Monday" |
| `search_records` | Searches records across a workspace. Requires at least one filter besides sort options. Filter by name text, tables (`tables_any`, `tables_not`, `tables_all`), teams, followers, creation date, and custom fields. | "Find records named 'Acme' in the Vendors table" / "Search for records created this week" |

##
**Write tools**

| Tool | Description | Example prompts |
|---|---|---|
| `create_tasks` | Creates one or more tasks immediately, with up to 50 tasks per call. Each task needs a project, parent task, or workspace and assignee context. Use `default_project` and `default_assignee` to share defaults across tasks. Supports sections, dates, descriptions, followers, and custom fields. Returns created tasks, failures, and a summary. Use an available task preview tool when the user asks to review before creating. | "Create tasks for each item in this list" / "Add three subtasks to this parent task" |
| `create_project` | Creates a project immediately, optionally with sections and tasks in those sections. If no team is provided, the server chooses a default team. Returns the project and results for section and task creation. Use an available project preview tool when the user asks to review before creating. | "Create a project for the Q4 launch with Backlog and In Progress sections" / "Set up a new project for the design team" |
| `create_task_from_template` | Lists a project's task templates when only `project_id` is provided, or starts creating a task from a template GID or an exact template name within that project. Name matching ignores case and requires one exact match. Creation is asynchronous. | "Show the task templates in this project" / "Create a task from the Bug Report template" |
| `create_project_from_template` | Starts creating a project from a project template. Find templates by name with `search_objects` and `resource_type: project_template`. Supports a project name, team, privacy, requested dates, and role assignments. Pass the desired team explicitly; omitting it does not inherit the template's team. Creation is asynchronous. | "Create an onboarding project from our standard template" |
| `update_project` | Updates project details, dates, owner, appearance, privacy, archive status, project custom-field values, sections, members, and custom-field settings for tasks. Adding members, making the project public, or changing default access requires explicit user confirmation. For those access changes, call without confirmation first to review the effects, then retry with confirmation after approval. Reports partial failures; some changes may still apply. | "Archive the completed launch project" / "Add a Review section to this project" |
| `update_tasks` | Updates one or more tasks, with up to 50 tasks per call. Supports names, assignees, dates, descriptions, completion, parent tasks, dependencies, dependents, project membership, followers, and custom fields. Reports successes and failures separately. A failed task may still have some changes applied. | "Mark these tasks as complete" / "Move these tasks to the Launch project" |
| `update_notifications` | Marks one or more of the authenticated user's Inbox notifications as read or unread. Pass notification GIDs from `get_notifications` and set `is_read` to `true` for read or `false` for unread. Available when notification tools are enabled for your session; check `tools/list`. | "Mark these notifications as read" / "Mark this notification as unread" |
| `delete_task` | Deletes a task and any subtasks that are not also members of another project. Use care when deleting tasks. | "Delete this duplicate task" |
| `add_comment` | Adds a task comment using exactly one of `text` or `html_text`. Supports mentions and pinned comments. Use for discussion, feedback, or context. Asana automatically logs actions such as assignments and status changes. | "Add a comment saying the design files are ready for review" / "Post a summary of today's decisions to this task" |
| `create_project_status_update` | Posts a status update to a project or portfolio. Requires a title, a color (`green`, `yellow`, `red`, `blue`, or `complete`), and exactly one of `text` or `html_text`. | "Post a green status update to the Q3 Roadmap project saying we are on track" / "Mark the Product Launch portfolio as at risk" |
| `create_table` | Creates a table in the workspace. Requires a name. Optionally pass `custom_field_settings` to set the table's initial custom field schema, using existing custom field GIDs or inline definitions for new fields. The table is created first, then each field is added in order. The table is still created if some fields fail, so check `failed` in the response. | "Create a Vendors table with a Status field and a Contract value field" |
| `update_table` | Renames a table and/or adds or removes individual custom fields from its schema. At least one of `name`, `add_custom_fields`, or `remove_custom_fields` is required. Each change affects only the fields it names; the schema is never replaced as a whole. | "Rename this table to Approved Vendors" / "Add a Renewal date field to this table" |
| `create_records` | Creates up to 50 records in one call. Each record requires a `name` and a `table`, and supports custom field values for fields already on the table. Returns created records, failures, and a summary. | "Add these vendors as records in the Vendors table" |
| `update_records` | Updates up to 50 records in one call. Each item requires a `record` GID plus a `name` and/or `custom_fields`. Items with neither are skipped. Reports successes and failures separately. | "Rename this record" / "Set the status of these records to Approved" |
| `delete_record` | Permanently deletes a record. This cannot be undone through this tool. | "Delete this duplicate record" |
| `add_record_comment` | Adds a comment to a record using exactly one of `text` or `html_text`. Supports pinned comments with `is_pinned`. | "Comment on this record that the contract was signed" |

##
**Interactive tools**

These tools display interactive search results or a draft for review before creation in clients that support interactive apps. Use `tools/list` to check the available preview tools and their schemas. Other clients can use the standard read and write tools.

| Tool | Description | Example prompts |
|---|---|---|
| `create_task_preview` | Drafts a task for review before creation. Supports project and section selection, subtasks, rich text descriptions, and editing after creation. | "Let me review a follow-up task before creating it" / "Preview a task with two subtasks" |
| `create_project_preview` | Drafts a project plan with sections and tasks for review before creation. Supports subtasks, rich text task descriptions, and editing after creation. | "Preview a project plan for our Q4 launch" / "Let me approve the website redesign plan before creating it" |
| `search_tasks_preview` | Searches tasks and displays results in an interactive UI. Supports text search, assignees, project, due and start date ranges, and completion status. | "Show me a visual list of tasks due this week" / "Find incomplete tasks assigned to me" |

##
**Tips for developers**

- **Migrating from V1?** Tool names in V2 no longer use the `asana_` prefix. Task creation and updates use `create_tasks` and `update_tasks`. Many tools that previously required a `workspaceGid` parameter no longer do, because workspace scope is set at authorization time. Review the [V2 changelog post](https://forum.asana.com/t/new-v2-mcp-server-now-generally-available/1122647) for the full list of what was renamed, consolidated, and dropped.
- **Use `tools/list` for current schemas.** Tool parameters may change over time. The authoritative source for parameter names, types, and constraints is the `tools/list` MCP command, not this page.
- **Check batch results.** Task creation, task updates, project creation with sections and tasks, project updates, record creation, record updates, table creation, and table updates can partially succeed. Inspect failures before retrying so you do not repeat changes that already succeeded.
- **Tokens are workspace-scoped.** When you authorize an MCP session, you select a specific workspace. All tool calls in that session are scoped to that workspace. To work across multiple workspaces, you need separate sessions.
- **MCP tokens do not work with the Asana REST API.** Tokens issued for MCP apps are valid only for the MCP server. For standard API access, create a separate app and authenticate through the standard OAuth flow.
- **App visibility can be limited to specific workspaces for private apps.** In the [Asana developer console](https://app.asana.com/0/my-apps) under "Manage distribution", you can control which workspaces' users are allowed to see your app.

- [Using Asana's MCP Server](https://developers.asana.com/docs/using-asanas-mcp-server): setup and connection guide for end users
- [Integrating with Asana's MCP Server](https://developers.asana.com/docs/integrating-with-asanas-mcp-server): OAuth app registration and authorization flow for developers
- [Connecting coding clients to Asana's V2 server](https://developers.asana.com/docs/connecting-mcp-clients-to-asanas-v2-server): setup instructions for Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, Codex, and more
- [API changelog](https://forum.asana.com/c/forum-en/api/api-changelog/204): subscribe for API and MCP updates
